quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your manager proposing a change to how your team handles customer enquiries.
options: I have noticed that enquiries often sit unanswered over the weekend, so I would like to suggest introducing a rota so that someone is always available to respond within twenty-four hours.
Dear Simon,
Subject: Suggestion to improve our customer enquiry process

Best regards,
Olivia Hart
quests.hint: The problem being solved is in the subject; the manager is addressed by first name; the observation and proposed solution form the body; 'BEST REGARDS' closes the internal suggestion politely.
quests.explanation: Backing up a suggestion with a specific observation ('enquiries sit unanswered over the weekend') is far more persuasive than simply saying the process needs improving. Proposing a concrete solution, not just naming a problem, shows initiative.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a recruiter after a successful interview, asking to discuss your possible start date.
options:
Yours sincerely,
Daniel Fox

Thank you for such an enjoyable interview yesterday - I remain very keen on the role and would like to discuss a possible start date, as I would need to give four weeks' notice to my current employer.
Dear Ms Okonkwo,
Subject: Following up on yesterday's interview - start date
quests.hint: The interview and topic are in the subject; the recruiter is addressed by name; your enthusiasm and a practical constraint (notice period) are in the body; the closing matches this named greeting.
quests.explanation: Mentioning your notice period upfront helps the employer plan realistically rather than assuming you can start immediately. Reaffirming your interest in the same sentence as a practical question keeps the tone positive rather than purely transactional.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your manager requesting approval to fund a professional course.
options:
Kind regards,
Priya Nair
I have found a part-time project management course that would directly support my work on the current rollout, and I would be grateful if the team could cover the £450 course fee.
Subject: Request to fund a project management course
Dear Hannah,
quests.hint: The course and purpose are in the subject; the manager is addressed by first name; the relevance to current work and the specific cost are in the body; 'KIND REGARDS' closes the funding request.
quests.explanation: Linking the course directly to a current project ('supports my work on the rollout') makes the request easier to justify than general career development. Stating the exact cost upfront saves the manager from having to ask before deciding.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your team organising a leaving collection for a retiring colleague.
options: Subject: Leaving collection for margaret's retirement

As most of you know, margaret is retiring at the end of the month after twenty-two years with the company, so I am collecting contributions for a gift and card - please let me know if you would like to contribute.
Dear Team,

Best wishes,
Jordan Lewis
quests.hint: The occasion and person are in the subject; the whole team is addressed together; the background and how to take part are in the body; 'BEST WISHES' closes warmly.
quests.explanation: Including a meaningful detail ('twenty-two years with the company') makes the collection feel personal rather than routine. Phrasing it as 'let me know if you would like to' rather than assuming participation keeps the invitation pressure-free.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your landlord asking permission to put up shelves in your rented flat.
options:
Yours sincerely,
Kai Andersson
Dear Mrs Oyelaran,
Subject: Permission request - putting up shelves in the living room
I would like to put up two small bookshelves in the living room and would be happy to use a professional fitter and fill any holes before I eventually move out, if that would put your mind at ease.
quests.hint: The request and room are in the subject; the landlord is addressed by name; the proposal and reassurance about restoring the wall are in the body; the closing matches this named greeting.
quests.explanation: Offering a reassurance ('fill any holes before I move out') before the landlord even raises a concern shows consideration and makes approval more likely. Small, specific requests like this are usually best asked directly rather than left until moving-out time.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write a casual email to an old friend you have lost touch with, suggesting you meet up.
options: Hi Sophie,
I know it's been ages since we last spoke, but I saw a photo of your new puppy online and realised how much I miss catching up with you - any chance you're free for a coffee sometime soon?

Can't wait to hear from you,
Ruby
Subject: It's been way too long!
quests.hint: A warm, informal exclamation opens the subject; an old friend is greeted casually by first name; the reason for getting back in touch and a low-pressure suggestion are in the body; a friendly sign-off closes it.
quests.explanation: Mentioning a specific, genuine reason for reaching out ('saw a photo of your new puppy') feels far warmer than a generic 'let's catch up' message. Suggesting something low-commitment like coffee makes it easy for your friend to say yes.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your GP surgery requesting a copy of your medical records.
options:
Yours faithfully,
Elena Vasquez
Subject: Request for a copy of my medical records
Dear Practice Manager,

I am moving abroad next month and will need to register with a new doctor, so I would be grateful if you could let me know how to request a copy of my full medical records and how long this usually takes.
quests.hint: The request and reason are in the subject; the practice manager is addressed by role, not name; the reason for moving and two practical questions are in the body; the closing must match this unnamed greeting.
quests.explanation: Explaining why you need the records ('registering with a new doctor abroad') helps the surgery process your request appropriately. Since you don't know the practice manager's name personally, 'Yours faithfully' is the correct closing here.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a university asking to defer the start of your course by one year.
options:
Yours faithfully,
Tobias Lindqvist
Dear Admissions Tutor,

I have been offered a place on the ba history course starting this september, but due to a family situation I need to stay close to home this year, so I would like to ask whether I could defer my place until the following september.
Subject: Request to defer my offer to next september
quests.hint: The course and request are in the subject; the tutor is addressed by role, not name; the offer, the reason, and the specific request are in the body; the closing must match this unnamed greeting.
quests.explanation: Giving a brief, honest reason ('a family situation') without oversharing personal details is the right level of detail for this kind of request. Naming the exact course helps admissions staff locate your application quickly.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a hotel asking if you can check in early for a special occasion.
options:
Many thanks,
Chidi Ezealor
Dear Reception Team,
Subject: Early check-in request for our anniversary stay
We are staying with you on 14 september to celebrate our tenth wedding anniversary and would love to check in early if a room happens to be ready, as our flight lands at 9 a.m.
quests.hint: The occasion and request are in the subject; the reception team is addressed; the date, the special reason, and the flight time are all in the body; 'MANY THANKS' closes the friendly request.
quests.explanation: Mentioning the occasion ('tenth wedding anniversary') often encourages hotel staff to go the extra mile if they can. Explaining why you're asking - an early flight - gives a genuine, practical reason rather than just a preference.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your manager proposing two fixed remote-working days per week.
options:
Best regards,
Amara Okafor
Subject: Proposal - two regular working-from-home days
Dear Richard,

Having now worked from home occasionally over the past few months, I have found I am most productive on focused tasks at home, so I would like to propose making tuesdays and thursdays my regular remote days going forward.
quests.hint: The proposal is in the subject; the manager is addressed by first name; the evidence from experience and the specific days requested are in the body; 'BEST REGARDS' closes professionally.
quests.explanation: Grounding the request in evidence ('found I am most productive on focused tasks at home') is more convincing than simply asking for flexibility. Proposing specific days, rather than a vague arrangement, makes it easy for the manager to say yes.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You run a small café. Write an email reply to a customer who left a critical review online.
options:
Warm regards,
Francesca Conti

Thank you for taking the time to share your experience - I am sorry to hear your order took so long on saturday, and I would love the chance to put this right with a complimentary coffee next time you visit.
Subject: Thank you for your feedback, mr davies
Dear Mr Davies,
quests.hint: A personal, non-defensive tone is set in the subject; the customer is addressed by name; the acknowledgement, apology, and gesture of goodwill are in the body; 'WARM REGARDS' closes warmly and professionally.
quests.explanation: Responding to criticism with genuine acknowledgement rather than excuses protects your business's reputation far more effectively. Offering a specific, small gesture ('a complimentary coffee') shows good faith without over-promising.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a gym asking if they offer a discount for a group of colleagues joining together.
options: Dear Membership Team,

A group of eight colleagues from my office are interested in joining together, so I would like to ask whether you offer a corporate or group rate, and if so, what documentation we would need to provide.

Kind regards,
Leo Bennett
Subject: Enquiry about corporate membership rates
quests.hint: The type of enquiry is in the subject; the team is addressed by role, not name; the group size and two related questions are in the body; 'KIND REGARDS' closes politely.
quests.explanation: Giving the exact group size ('eight colleagues') allows the gym to quote an accurate rate rather than a generic one. Asking about paperwork in the same email avoids a frustrating back-and-forth once the group is ready to sign up.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your bank disputing a fee you believe was charged incorrectly.
options: Subject: Disputed charge - £25 overdraft fee on 3 july

I noticed a £25 overdraft fee on my account dated 3 july, but according to my own records my balance did not go below zero that week, so I would be grateful if you could look into this and refund the charge if it was applied in error.

Yours faithfully,
Martina Kovacs
Dear Customer Services,
quests.hint: The disputed amount and date are in the subject; customer services is addressed by role, not name; your evidence and the specific request are in the body; the closing must match this unnamed greeting.
quests.explanation: Stating your own records ('my balance did not go below zero') gives the bank a concrete reason to investigate rather than dismiss your query. Asking for a refund 'if it was applied in error' is fair and avoids sounding accusatory before the facts are confirmed.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a university library asking for an extension on a book you need for your dissertation.
options: Subject: Renewal request - reference copy needed for dissertation
Dear Library Team,

I still need the copy of 'economic history of europe' that is due back tomorrow, as several chapters are essential to my dissertation, so I would like to ask whether I could renew it for a further two weeks.

Kind regards,
Samuel Otieno
quests.hint: The book and deadline are in the subject; the library team is addressed; the reason it's needed and the specific renewal period are in the body; 'KIND REGARDS' closes the polite request.
quests.explanation: Naming the exact book and explaining why it matters ('essential to my dissertation') gives library staff a clear reason to prioritise your renewal. Asking for a specific length of extension is easier to approve than an open-ended request.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your landlord proposing a smaller rent increase than the one they suggested.
options: Thank you for letting me know about the proposed increase - I understand costs are rising, but a jump of £150 a month would be difficult for me right now, so I would like to propose an increase of £75 instead, with a review again next year.
Dear Mr Abara,
Subject: Response to proposed rent increase

Yours sincerely,
Freya Johansson
quests.hint: The topic is stated plainly in the subject; the landlord is addressed by name; acknowledgement of their position, your constraint, and a specific counter-proposal are in the body; the closing matches this named greeting.
quests.explanation: Opening with understanding ('I understand costs are rising') before disagreeing makes a counter-offer far more likely to be well received. Proposing a specific figure and a future review date shows you are negotiating in good faith, not simply refusing.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a former manager asking if they would write you a professional recommendation.
options:
Warmly,
Noah Ferreira
Subject: Would you be willing to write me a recommendation?
Dear Claire,

I am currently applying for senior analyst roles and would be very grateful if you would be willing to write me a short recommendation, particularly reflecting on the reporting system I built during my time on your team.
quests.hint: The request is stated directly in the subject; the former manager is addressed warmly by first name; the context and a specific achievement to mention are in the body; 'WARMLY' closes on a personal note.
quests.explanation: Suggesting a specific achievement to mention ('the reporting system I built') makes it much easier for a busy former manager to write something detailed rather than generic. A warm, familiar closing suits someone you worked closely with.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write a group email to colleagues coordinating a surprise leaving party for a teammate.
options: Subject: Shhh - surprise party for jake on friday!
As you know, jake is leaving for his new job next week, so we are planning a surprise gathering at the rose and crown at 5.30 on friday - please keep it quiet and let me know if you can make it.

See you there,
Mia Thompson
Hi Everyone,
quests.hint: An urgent, secretive tone is set in the subject; the whole group is greeted informally; the plan, location, time, and request for secrecy are in the body; a casual sign-off closes it.
quests.explanation: Capital letters and an exclamation mark in the subject line suit an exciting, secretive group message like this one - a tone that would feel wrong in a formal email. Explicitly asking people to 'keep it quiet' is essential when planning a surprise.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your car insurance company asking to add a named driver to your policy.
options: Dear Policy Services Team,

Kind regards,
Isobel Mackenzie
Subject: Request to add a named driver - policy ref: cv88214

I would like to add my partner to my policy as a named driver from next month, and I would be grateful if you could let me know what information you need from me and whether this will affect my monthly premium.
quests.hint: The policy reference and request are in the subject; the team is addressed by role, not name; the specific request and two follow-up questions are in the body; 'KIND REGARDS' closes politely.
quests.explanation: Including your policy reference number in the subject lets the insurer pull up your account immediately. Asking about the effect on your premium in the same email avoids being surprised by a price change later.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your manager requesting a private meeting to discuss your current workload.
options: Subject: Could we find time to discuss my workload?

Over the last few weeks I have been struggling to keep up with both the client accounts and the new onboarding project, and I would really appreciate a chance to sit down with you and work out a more manageable balance.

Best regards,
Theo Marsden
Dear Andrea,
quests.hint: A gentle, non-alarming question opens the subject; the manager is addressed by first name; the specific pressures and a constructive request for a conversation are in the body; 'BEST REGARDS' closes professionally.
quests.explanation: Naming the two specific pressures ('client accounts' and 'the onboarding project') helps your manager understand the problem immediately rather than guessing. Framing the request as wanting to 'work out a balance' together keeps the tone collaborative, not confrontational.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your child's school explaining a change in family circumstances that may affect them.
options:
Yours sincerely,
Beatrix Solberg
Dear Mrs Abiodun,

I wanted to let you know that luca's grandfather, who he is very close to, was recently admitted to hospital, and he has seemed quieter than usual at home - I would be grateful if his teachers could keep a gentle eye on him.
Subject: A change at home that may affect luca this term
quests.hint: A sensitive summary is in the subject; the teacher is addressed by name; the situation, its effect at home, and a gentle request are in the body; the closing matches this named, caring tone.
quests.explanation: Giving the school just enough context to understand the child's behaviour, without excessive detail, respects both privacy and the teacher's need to know. Asking staff to 'keep a gentle eye' rather than demanding special treatment sets a reasonable, collaborative tone.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a conference organiser asking whether a discounted rate is available for students.
options:
Many thanks,
Omar Sheikh
Subject: Does your conference offer a student rate?
Dear Events Team,

I am a full-time master's student with a strong interest in attending your conference in october, but the standard ticket is beyond my budget, so I wanted to ask whether a discounted student rate is available.
quests.hint: The direct question is in the subject; the team is addressed by role, not name; your status, genuine interest, and the specific request are in the body; 'MANY THANKS' closes the polite enquiry.
quests.explanation: Being upfront and specific ('the standard ticket is beyond my budget') rather than vague is a confident, reasonable way to ask about a discount. Mentioning genuine interest in the conference, not just the price, shows this isn't only about the discount.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write a thank-you email to a mentor who recently gave you valuable career advice.
options:
With gratitude,
Isaac Webb
Dear Grace,

I just wanted to say thank you for taking the time to talk through my career options last week - your suggestion to speak to the operations team directly has already led to a really useful conversation.
Subject: Thank you for your advice last week
quests.hint: A simple thank-you is in the subject; the mentor is addressed warmly by first name; the specific advice and its result are in the body; 'WITH GRATITUDE' closes on a genuinely appreciative note.
quests.explanation: Mentioning the specific outcome of the advice ('already led to a really useful conversation') shows a mentor that their time made a real difference, not just that you were being polite. A closing like 'With gratitude' fits a heartfelt thank-you better than a routine one like 'Kind regards'.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your letting agency reporting a pest problem in your rented flat.
options: Over the past week I have seen clear signs of mice in the kitchen, including droppings near the cooker, and I would be grateful if you could arrange for pest control to visit as soon as possible.
Subject: Pest control needed - mice in the kitchen

Yours faithfully,
Adaora Nwosu
Dear Property Management Team,
quests.hint: The problem and location are in the subject; the team is addressed by role, not name; the evidence and the urgent request are in the body; the closing must match this unnamed greeting.
quests.explanation: Describing specific evidence ('droppings near the cooker') rather than just saying 'we have mice' gives the agency clear proof to act on quickly. Pest problems are usually treated as urgent, so it's reasonable to ask for a prompt visit.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a company politely asking for feedback after your job application was rejected.
options: Thank you for letting me know the outcome of my application for the data analyst role - while I am naturally disappointed, I would really value any feedback you could share to help me improve for future applications.
Dear Mr Okafor,
Subject: Request for feedback on my recent application

Yours sincerely,
Hannah Osei-tutu
quests.hint: A polite, professional request is in the subject; the recruiter is addressed by name; gracious acknowledgement of the decision and a specific ask for feedback are in the body; the closing matches this named greeting.
quests.explanation: Accepting the outcome gracefully before asking for feedback keeps the door open for future opportunities with the same company. Framing the request around self-improvement ('to help me improve') rather than challenging the decision comes across as mature and professional.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You run a small business. Write an email to a supplier asking to extend your payment terms from 14 to 30 days.
options: We have valued working with you over the past year and our orders have grown steadily, so as we scale up I would like to ask whether you would consider moving our payment terms from 14 to 30 days, in line with most of our other suppliers.
Dear Mr Patterson,
Subject: Request to extend our payment terms to 30 days

Best regards,
Yusuf Ibrahim
quests.hint: The specific request is in the subject; the supplier contact is addressed by name; the relationship history, the reason, and the comparison to other suppliers are in the body; 'BEST REGARDS' closes professionally.
quests.explanation: Opening with the positive relationship ('valued working with you') before making a request softens what could otherwise feel like a demand. Comparing the request to standard industry practice ('in line with most of our other suppliers') makes it feel reasonable rather than one-sided.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your fitness instructor explaining an injury and asking for modified exercises.
options: Subject: Request for modified exercises due to a knee injury
Dear Coach Reyes,

Many thanks,
Clara Dubois

I hurt my knee playing football at the weekend and my physiotherapist has advised me to avoid deep squats for the next few weeks, so I wanted to let you know before thursday's class in case you can suggest alternatives.
quests.hint: The injury is named in the subject; the instructor is addressed by name and title; the cause, the medical advice, and a practical heads-up are in the body; 'MANY THANKS' closes appreciatively.
quests.explanation: Mentioning professional advice ('my physiotherapist has advised') gives the instructor a clear, medically-grounded reason to adapt the session for you. Letting them know before the class, rather than mentioning it on arrival, gives them time to plan alternatives.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a nursery asking about the settling-in process for your child before they start.
options:
Kind regards,
Wendy And Marcus Tan
Dear Nursery Team,
Subject: Question about the settling-in process for new children

Our daughter will be starting with you in september and, as this will be her first time away from us regularly, we would like to ask how the settling-in sessions work and how many we would typically need to attend together beforehand.
quests.hint: The purpose is in the subject; the nursery team is addressed; the context (first time away from parents) and two specific questions are in the body; 'KIND REGARDS' closes as a couple.
quests.explanation: Explaining that this is your child's 'first time away from us regularly' helps staff understand the family's needs, not just the logistics. Asking how many sessions are typical shows you are planning ahead rather than leaving it to the last minute.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your team suggesting an idea for the next office social event.
options: Hi Team,

Let me know what you think,
Felix Romano
Subject: Idea for our next team social - escape room?

After a few people mentioned wanting to do something different this time, I looked into a local escape room that can take groups of up to twelve, and I think it could be a fun way to mix up our usual pub trips.
quests.hint: A specific idea is proposed right in the subject; the team is greeted informally; the origin of the idea and a practical detail (group size) are in the body; a casual, inviting sign-off closes it.
quests.explanation: Referencing that 'a few people mentioned wanting something different' shows the idea responds to real feedback, not just personal preference. Including a practical detail like group capacity shows you've already done some groundwork, making the idea easier to say yes to.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to your manager formally requesting two weeks of unpaid leave for a family matter.
options:
Yours sincerely,
Petra Novak

Due to a serious family matter I need to attend to in person, I would like to formally request two weeks of unpaid leave from 14 october, and I am happy to discuss how my workload can be covered beforehand.
Subject: Request for two weeks' unpaid leave
Dear Mr Whittaker,
quests.hint: The request and duration are in the subject; the manager is addressed by name; the reason (kept private), the exact dates, and an offer to help with handover are in the body; the closing matches this named greeting.
quests.explanation: Keeping the reason general ('a serious family matter') is entirely acceptable - you are not obliged to share private details to justify a leave request. Offering to help plan handover cover, rather than waiting to be asked, shows responsibility even while dealing with a difficult situation.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a local newspaper suggesting a positive story about a community project.
options: Subject: Story suggestion - community garden turning one year old

Yours faithfully,
Rosalind Pike
Dear Editor,

Our community garden on elm street is celebrating its first birthday this month, having grown from an empty plot into a space used by over forty local families, and I thought it might make a lovely local story.
quests.hint: The story idea is in the subject; the editor is addressed by role, not name; the background and a specific, uplifting statistic are in the body; the closing must match this unnamed greeting.
quests.explanation: Including a concrete statistic ('over forty local families') helps an editor quickly judge the story's local interest and scale. Suggesting a story rather than demanding coverage keeps the tone appropriately modest for a first approach.
